hookups.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('Camping is primitive, temporary and dispersed. There are no established campsites and no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations).'), read 2026-10-21

facilities.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations)'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' C.F. Phelps lists Primitive Camping among its activities; DWR describes Kelly's Ford as 'a parking area and ramp for small boats and canoes ... on the Culpeper side of the Rappahannock'.

booking.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ + https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/c-f-phelps/ (Recreational Opportunities: 'Primitive Camping'; Facilities), read 2026-10-21

summary: Confirmed on DWR's C.F. Phelps page that primitive camping is still allowed on the WMA, and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization. Not stated: season, anything camping-specific at Kelly's Ford. Note left as is.
flags: Waterfront + criteria lead: entry is riverfront at the Kelly's Ford parking area, which DWR describes as 'a parking area and ramp for small boats and canoes' (map shows the ramp at the lot). DWR's statewide rule (https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/): 'It is unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility (building, boat ramp, etc.)'. Camping in this ramp lot looks unlawful, and a legal spot 300 ft from the ramp is unlikely to be on the river.
